# Convert MP4 to WebM

- Route: `/tools/convert-mp4-to-webm`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `video`
- Slug: `convert-mp4-to-webm`

## Summary

Re-encode MP4 into a smaller, open VP9 WebM that is perfect for fast-loading web video. (Video tools)

## Details

WebM is the open video format built for the web. With VP9 video and Opus audio it delivers smaller files than MP4 at the same quality, which means faster page loads for embedded video. Converting your MP4 to WebM is the right move when you control the player — modern browsers all support it natively.
### What it does
- Converts MP4 (H.264) to WebM (VP9 + Opus).
- Locks the output to WebM for consistent open-web embeds.
- Typically produces a smaller file than the MP4 at the same visual quality.
- Shorten or shrink the clip and choose a quality preset before the WebM is made.
### How to use it
1. Upload your MP4: Drop in an .mp4 file.
2. Output is locked to WebM: WebM (VP9 + Opus) is preset for this tool.
3. Convert: We re-encode H.264 to VP9 and AAC to Opus.
4. Download: Save a smaller .webm for the web.
### Supported formats
- Input: mp4, mov, m4v
- Output: webm
- Output is locked to WebM (VP9 + Opus, or VP8 + Vorbis if VP9/Opus is unavailable).
### Technical details
- WebM output uses VP9 video with Opus audio where available, falling back to VP8 + Vorbis on FFmpeg builds without VP9/Opus.
- VP9 encoding is slower than H.264 but yields ~25-50% smaller files at comparable quality.
- Use the <video> tag with both a WebM and an MP4 source so browsers pick the best one they support.
### Use cases
- Website hero video: Serve a small, fast-loading background or hero clip.
- Open-web embeds: Embed video without proprietary codec concerns.
- Bandwidth savings: Cut delivery size for high-traffic pages.
- HTML5 <video>: Provide a WebM source alongside an MP4 fallback.
### FAQ
Q: How do I convert MP4 to WebM?
A: Upload your .mp4 file and click convert — the output is already set to WebM.
Q: Is WebM smaller than MP4?
A: At the same visual quality, VP9 WebM is usually 25-50% smaller than H.264 MP4.
Q: Do all browsers support WebM?
A: All modern browsers do. For older browsers, provide an MP4 fallback in your <video> tag.
Q: Why is WebM encoding slower?
A: VP9 is more computationally intensive than H.264. The payoff is a smaller file.
